scope: ProductReview page labelled fourth-generation ZM PHEV (2022–2026), four self-selected posts. The visible aggregate includes an explicit 2021 GSR / August 2021 purchase review describing 49-km EV range, so the page is NOT a clean ZM-only sample. No isolated MY26 22.7-kWh subset.
summary: Contributors praise electric driving and family space, but generation contamination limits applicability: the displayed 4.7/5 from four posts cannot be treated as four confirmed current-generation owners. No defensible clean-subset rating was calculated.
positiveThemes: Smooth electric acceleration and quiet running
Sliding second row and space for family use
Petrol backup alongside regular electric driving
negativeThemes: Some cabin noise and startup/infotainment annoyances
Third row described by one owner as occasional-use space
Economy varies with charging and driving mode

scope: ProductReview Sealion 6 page labelled 2024–2026, mixed variants. Some posts rate dealer/lease experiences as well as the vehicle; nine self-selected posts.
summary: Owners praise comfort, equipment and charged-up economy. Dealer and warranty experiences vary sharply; individual complaints are not verified fault-frequency evidence.
positiveThemes: Quiet, comfortable driving and plentiful equipment
Low petrol use when regularly charged
negativeThemes: Individual reports of panel fit, wipers or charging quirks
Soft suspension and limited boot space noted

scope: ProductReview T33 Ti e-POWER page labelled 2023–2026; this is a four-post Ti subset, not all e-POWER trims or the mixed-petrol X-Trail aggregate.
summary: Visible owners value the smooth electric-motor drive. One detailed MY25 owner reports technology and after-sales frustrations; check the actual build and equipment.
negativeThemes: MY25 app/connectivity and map-update frustrations in one report
Individual concerns about engine noise, audio or lack of spare

scope: ProductReview XA50 FWD 2.5L Hybrid page: 18 contributions across GX, GXL and Cruiser, including a hire-car report and pre-2021 cars. Not the sixth-generation 2026 RAV4.
summary: The FWD hybrid subset is a closer match than the AWD aggregate. Contributors praise economy and practicality, with mixed views on cabin quality, noise and technology. Self-selected posts cannot establish reliability.
positiveThemes: Hybrid economy in urban and mixed use
Owners appreciate the original capped-service period
negativeThemes: Road and wind noise at highway speeds
Some owners regard equipment or finish as poor value

scope: ProductReview AWD Hybrid page labelled 2021–2026, seven posts across GX/GXL/Grande; not the older petrol Kluger aggregate. At least one post is marked incentivised.
summary: Owners describe a spacious, quiet family car but disagree about finish, equipment and support. Seven posts cannot settle Toyota or Kluger reliability.
positiveThemes: Roomy cabin and smooth, quiet driving
Economy praised against previous large family cars
negativeThemes: Lane-assist intrusiveness and a sunroof creak in one report
Individual dissatisfaction with warranty handling and equipment

scope: ProductReview MQ4 page labelled 2020–2026: MIXED petrol, diesel, HEV and PHEV; includes independent expert posts. The aggregate is not a Sorento hybrid reliability rating.
summary: Broader MQ4 feedback praises comfort and equipment, with some after-sales complaints. Hybrid-only evidence is sparse: FWD HEV has two posts including an expert; PHEV has one expert post, not an owner sample.
positiveThemes: Comfortable ride and family accommodation across mixed variants
Equipment and perceived interior quality praised
Owners value the long transferable warranty
negativeThemes: Mixed-variant reports of service communication and repair delays
One HEV owner reports seat discomfort; do a full family test drive
